title: Portability: projection and copied-project shadow matrix
description: Objective: exercise the shipped legacy importer, task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8's real daemon shadow adapter, and public compareShadowProjections over a copied-project corpus. Produce exact PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN advisory outcomes while proving the source copy and durable current store remain byte-for-byte untouched.
definitionOfDone: A nonempty copied-project corpus is read through the production legacy importer and compared with the production daemon shadow adapter at one captured store horizon; the test never constructs the current ShadowProjection itself.

Generated matched, changed, absent-current, absent-legacy, unmapped-field, malformed, and unreadable cases assert a positive case count plus the exact mismatch kind/disposition or stable refusal code/layer; one full exact-match control yields zero mismatches.
Every case records the checkout source commit and canonical fixture manifest digest, and repeated runs over unchanged bytes produce identical ordered comparison bytes.
Before/after SHA-256, file-size, and mtime inventories for the copied corpus plus raw SQLite event/decision counts and database bytes/mtime are identical, including every refusal arm.
Focused integration tests execute with nonzero test counts on Windows and use native temp/path handling that is portable to Linux and macOS.
taskRails: Use only public package roots and the real production surface under test; no test helper may reimplement a projection, provider decision, transport handshake, or host adapter.
Every refusal/failure arm asserts the exact stable reason code and refusing layer; generated matrices assert a positive case count and include an accepted control so refusal-only suites cannot pass.
All fixtures and results are advisory/read-only: no imported state may activate, mutate durable authority, select a best tool, or perform cutover.
Use TDD and mutation-drill the production surface so a named assertion reddens; keep owned files focused and stage/commit only explicit paths.
Hard-depend on task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8; missing LINK/BLOCKER authority must remain UNKNOWN/refused, never filled by fixture assumptions.
Own only the projection matrix test and at most two focused fixture/helper files under tests/integration/portability.

implementationPlan.description:
THE CORPUS: create tests/integration/portability/shadow-corpus-fixtures.ts (helper 1 of the 2 task rail 6 permits).
It declares a NONEMPTY copied-project corpus as data plus the case table, and contains no assertions and no store access.
- CORPUS: legacy source records covering at least a claim with links, a claim with `links: []`, a HISTORICAL claim and a SUSPENDED claim. The last two matter because the daemon mapper emits a BLOCKER only for SUSPENDED, and `links: []` is KNOWN-EMPTY rather than unavailable — that distinction is the semantic hinge of the whole adapter and a corpus that never exercises it cannot see a regression in it.
- MATERIALISATION: write the corpus to a temp directory as real files, so `buildSourceManifest` and `decodeLegacySources` walk bytes on disk exactly as they would for a real copied project. A corpus held only in memory would skip the manifest digest this task must record.
- CASE TABLE: one row per DoD-2 case — matched, changed, absent-current, absent-legacy, unmapped-field, malformed, unreadable — each declaring its expected mismatch kind and disposition, or its expected refusal code AND refusing layer. Import `SHADOW_MISMATCH_KINDS`, `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS` and `SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS` from the @moe/import root and `IMPORT_SHADOW_REFUSAL_CODES` / `IMPORT_SHADOW_READ_LAYER` from the @moe/daemon root rather than spelling any of them locally; a locally spelled code is a second vocabulary that drifts, and the drift shows up as a green test asserting something production no longer emits.
- Export the case count so step 4 can assert it is POSITIVE before running anything.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 — CORPUS AND CASE TABLE LANDED in `tests/integration/portability/shadow-corpus-fixtures.ts` (helper 1 of the 2 rail 6 permits). Data only: no assertions, no store access, no projection logic. Typechecks clean through the directory's own project config — 0 diagnostics naming the file.

THE ON-DISK FORMAT WAS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, because a corpus in the wrong shape would refuse at the decoder and every downstream case would be testing the decoder instead of the adapter:
- `SUPPORTED_SOURCE_FAMILIES` (legacy-decoder.ts:38) is exactly `{skills: "skill", tasks: "task"}`, and `decodeEntry` requires the path to end `.json` under one of those directories.
- `RECORD_ENVELOPE_KEYS` (:50) is `["id", "legacyId", "time"]`; `readPayload` (:159) keeps everything else, in the bytes' own key order. So the payload is whatever is not envelope.
- `applyImport`'s `claimFrom` (:82-90): `principal` is `payload.owner` or the literal `"UNKNOWN"`; status is `SUSPENDED` when `payload.held === true`, else `HISTORICAL`. `linksFrom` (:95+): `payload.parent` (string) emits a CONTAINS link, `payload.dependsOn` emits RELATED links.
- The daemon mapper (import-shadow-mapper.ts:77-80) emits a BLOCKER entity ONLY for `status === "SUSPENDED"`, carrying `basis: "SUSPENDED_CLAIM"` and `holder: claim.principal`. Its own comment says a HISTORICAL claim emitting none is a FACT about that claim, not a gap.

THE CORPUS IS FOUR CLAIMS CHOSEN TO SEPARATE TWO THINGS THAT ARE EASY TO CONFOUND:
- `task-linked` — HISTORICAL with BOTH a parent (CONTAINS) and a dependsOn (RELATED).
- `task-empty-links` — HISTORICAL with NO parent and NO dependsOn: links are KNOWN-EMPTY.
- `task-historical` — HISTORICAL but WITH a link. This one exists specifically so "historical" is not confounded with "has no links"; without it, a regression that keyed BLOCKER emission off link-count instead of status would still look correct.
- `task-suspended` — `held: true`, the only claim that yields a BLOCKER.
That gives all four combinations of {HISTORICAL, SUSPENDED} x {has links, known-empty}, which is what makes the step-5 known-empty assertion and the step-9 drill 3 (emit a BLOCKER for HISTORICAL too) able to fail.

MATERIALISATION IS REAL FILES. `materialiseCorpus(root)` writes each document as pretty-printed JSON under `tasks/`, creating directories as needed, so `buildSourceManifest` and `decodeLegacySources` walk bytes on disk. An in-memory corpus would never produce the manifest digest DoD 3 requires me to record.

NOTHING IS SPELLED LOCALLY. Every expected value is imported from its owning root: `SHADOW_MISMATCH_KINDS` and `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS` from `@moe/import`, `IMPORT_SHADOW_REFUSAL_CODES` and `IMPORT_SHADOW_READ_LAYER` from `@moe/daemon`. Dispositions in particular are LOOKED UP — the `mismatch()` helper does `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS[kind]` rather than restating the pairing, so a case cannot assert a disposition production no longer maps to that kind. Confirmed the production map while writing it: ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT/FIELD_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT/FIELD_DIFFERS -> NEEDS_RECONCILIATION; ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_LEGACY/FIELD_ABSENT_ON_LEGACY/FIELD_UNMAPPED -> UNKNOWN.

SEVEN CASES, one per DoD-2 row, each tagged with its row name. `MATRIX_CASE_COUNT` is exported so step 4 can assert POSITIVE before anything runs, and `REQUIRED_ROWS` is exported so the suite can assert every DoD row appears at least once — a count alone would pass if two cases covered the same row and another were dropped.

FILENAME COLLISION CHECK: this directory already holds the peer's `portability-cases.ts` / `portability-harness.ts` (untracked, task-efe5465f) and the tracked `provider-shadow-matrix.test.ts` / `shadow-matrix-arms.ts` / `shadow-matrix-cases.ts`. `shadow-corpus-fixtures.ts` collides with none.

implementationPlan.description:
THE HARNESS: create tests/integration/portability/shadow-corpus-harness.ts (helper 2 of 2). Lifecycle and evidence capture only — no assertions, no expected values, no projection logic.
- COPY AND INVENTORY: copy the corpus into `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-shadow-"))` and capture a BEFORE inventory for every corpus file: SHA-256, byte size and mtime. Provide the same capture as an AFTER call. Digest AND size AND mtime for EVERY entry, never a sample — a write that restores identical content still moves mtime, and that is the point.
- REAL STORE: `SqliteEventStore.openForProject(dbPath, projectId)`. NOT `open`: a handle opened without a project refuses every commit with PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED, which the neighbouring tests/integration/import suite already documents. Capture raw event count, command-decision count, database file size and mtime, before and after.
- PRODUCTION INGEST: a helper that takes a corpus directory and runs the PRODUCTION chain — `buildSourceManifest` -> `decodeLegacySources` -> `applyImport` -> `commitLegacyImport` — returning the manifest digest and the `LegacyImportFacts` the importer derived. Nothing here may hand-build an `ImportCommitInput` or an event payload; the byte-identity claim is about what the importer drafted.
- TEARDOWN in a `finally` on every path: close every store, remove every temp root. A held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker with an error that looks unrelated to the test.
- Native path handling throughout (`join`, `tmpdir`), so the suite is portable to Linux and macOS while being exercised on Windows (DoD item 5).
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — HARNESS LANDED in `tests/integration/portability/shadow-corpus-harness.ts` (helper 2 of 2). Lifecycle and evidence capture only: no assertions, no expected values, no projection logic. Typechecks clean through the directory's project config — 0 diagnostics naming either of my two files.

INVENTORY captures DIGEST **and** SIZE **and** MTIME for EVERY file, never a sample, via a recursive walk whose keys are POSIX-normalised (`relative(...).split(sep).join("/")`) so the key set is host-independent. All three matter for different reasons, recorded in the file: an identical-content rewrite moves ONLY mtime, and a truncation that happens to collide on a prefix moves only size. Digest alone would miss both.

STORE FACTS: raw event count and command-decision count are obtained by PAGING `readEventsAfter`/`readCommandDecisionsAfter` to exhaustion rather than reading one page — a single 100-item page would silently cap the count and make a write look like no change. Plus database file size and mtime from `statSync`.

`openForProject`, NOT `open`, as the plan requires: a handle opened without a project refuses every commit with PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED, and a suite built on `open` would see every ingest refuse and could mistake that for a shadow verdict.

TEARDOWN IS TOTAL. `withCorpus` keeps a list of every store it opened and closes ALL of them in a `finally` BEFORE `rmSync` removes the tree. A handle held across `rmSync` throws EPERM on Windows and kills the vitest worker with an error that looks unrelated to the test.

=== ONE DESIGN CHANGE I MADE, AND WHY IT IS BETTER THAN WHAT I FIRST WROTE ===
My first version had a `legacyFactsOnly()` helper that ran `applyImport` against a STUBBED store port so it could derive facts without committing them. Typecheck rejected it — `ImportStorePort` (import-apply.ts:63) declares exactly `commit(input): ImportCommitOutcome`, not `readEvents` — and that was the right rejection to take seriously rather than to satisfy with a cast. `applyImport` only try/catches around `input.store.commit(...)` and ignores its return, so a no-op port WOULD have "worked", and that is precisely the problem: a fixture-supplied sink standing in for the durable writer is the shape task rail 1 warns about, and the ABSENT-CURRENT arm's whole value is that the current side really came from durable rows.
REPLACED WITH: `context.openScratchStore(name)`, a second REAL project-bound store in the same temp root, registered for the same teardown. Arms that need legacy facts the main store never saw now ingest the FULL corpus into a throwaway store and compare against a main store holding only a subset. The entire chain stays production — `buildSourceManifest` -> `decodeLegacySources` -> `applyImport` -> `commitLegacyImport` — with no stub port anywhere.

`ingestCorpus(corpusRoot, store, keep?)` runs that chain and returns `{facts, manifest, manifestDigest, records}`, where `facts` is `{claims, links}` taken from the committed `ImportReport` — the importer's OWN derivation. Nothing hand-builds an `ImportCommitInput` or an event payload; the byte-identity claim is about what the importer drafted. The optional `keep` predicate filters DECODED records before the commit, which is how the subset arms are built without touching the corpus on disk. Manifest and decode refusals throw with their exact code and layer rather than returning a degraded result, so a broken fixture can never masquerade as a shadow verdict.

PORTABILITY (DoD 5): every path is composed with `join` and rooted at `tmpdir()`; no separator is written literally and no drive letter is assumed. Exercised on Windows, correct on Linux and macOS.

implementationPlan.description:
THE ACCEPTED CONTROL, first, in tests/integration/portability/projection-shadow-matrix.test.ts.
Before any case runs, assert the generated case count is POSITIVE and that every declared case kind appears at least once — a generated matrix that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing, which is why the epic rail names it explicitly.
Then the full exact-match control required by DoD item 2: ingest the whole corpus through the production chain, then call `compareImportShadow(store, { manifestDigest }, legacyFacts)` from the @moe/daemon root with the SAME facts the importer derived. Assert `comparison.mismatches` is EMPTY and `comparison.refusals` is empty.
THE TEST MUST NEVER CONSTRUCT THE CURRENT PROJECTION (DoD item 1, task rail 1). It never calls `projectLegacyImport` for the current side, never assembles a `ShadowProjection` literal, and never substitutes BoardProjection or WorkClaimLedger. `compareImportShadow` reads the current side itself through `readImportShadowProjection` at one captured horizon; the suite's only job is to supply the legacy facts and read the verdict.
This control is what keeps every refusal case below honest: a refusal-only suite where nothing can ever match would report every refusal correctly and still prove nothing (task rail 2).
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 — ACCEPTED CONTROL GREEN. `Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 5 passed (5)`, run from PowerShell.

THIS IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE RESULT SO FAR, because it exercises the whole chain end to end for the first time: corpus materialised as real files -> `buildSourceManifest` -> `decodeLegacySources` -> `applyImport` -> `commitLegacyImport` -> `compareImportShadow` reading the durable rows back. Zero mismatches, zero refusals. Everything I measured statically in step 1 is now confirmed dynamically.

**THE VACUOUS-GREEN HAZARD IS CONFIRMED CLOSED, not just assumed.** The governor's reopen note carried it forward, and step 1 found `commitLegacyImport` on disk. This step proves it operationally: `result.current.entities.length > 0`. The current side really carries entities read from durable rows, so a zero-mismatch verdict here means agreement rather than "both sides were empty".

THREE GUARDS ON THE CASE TABLE, run before any case:
- `MATRIX_CASE_COUNT > 0`, the positive-count assertion epic rail 2 names.
- Every DoD-2 row covered, asserted as a SET equality against `REQUIRED_ROWS` rather than by count. A count alone still passes if two cases cover one row while another row is silently dropped — the exact way a matrix shrinks without anyone noticing.
- Every case name distinct, since a duplicated name halves a sweep while the length still reads correct.

THE CONTROL HAS A COMPANION THAT MAKES IT MEAN SOMETHING. "Zero mismatches" is also what two EMPTY projections produce, so a second test asserts the comparison was over real work before trusting the first: `claims.length > 0`, `links.length > 0`, `manifestDigest` matches `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`, and `current.entities.length > 0`. Without that pair, the control is a green light wired to nothing — which is precisely the failure task rail 2 describes for refusal-only suites, in its mirror form.

DoD 1 AND TASK RAIL 1 HELD STRUCTURALLY. The suite calls `compareImportShadow` and reads `.comparison`; it never calls `projectLegacyImport`, never assembles a `ShadowProjection` literal, and never touches BoardProjection or WorkClaimLedger. The adapter reads the current side itself at one horizon it captures. Step 11 greps for all three to confirm this rather than trusting my intent, and step 9's tautology drill is what proves the comparison is not one function against itself.

ADVISORY POSTURE asserted on the accepted arm already (`advisoryOnly: true`, `authority: "NONE"`), which step 8 extends to both arms.

CONTRACT SHAPES CONFIRMED while writing, so later arms assert against the real thing: `compareImportShadow(store, request, legacyFacts)` returns `ImportShadowCompared` `{advisoryOnly, authority, comparison, current, legacy, ok:true}` or `ImportShadowRefused` `{advisoryOnly, authority, code, detail, layer, ok:false}`; `ShadowComparison` is `{mismatches, refusals, version}`; `ShadowMismatch` carries `{currentValue, disposition, entityId, entityKind, field, legacyValue, mismatchKind}`. Notably `ImportShadowRefused.code` is typed `ImportEventRefusalCode | ImportShadowRefusalCode` and `.layer` is `ImportRefusalLayer | ImportShadowReadLayer` — the TYPE itself admits two layers, which is why step 6 pins the layer on every refusal arm rather than only the code.

A helper `compared()` narrows the union and, on an unexpected refusal, throws with the refusal's OWN code and layer — so a broken arm reports what production actually said instead of a generic "expected true to be false".

implementationPlan.description:
THE MISMATCH ARMS — DoD item 2's generated matched/changed/absent-current/absent-legacy/unmapped-field cases, each asserting the EXACT mismatch kind AND its disposition, read from `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS` rather than hand-asserted.
- CHANGED: alter one CLAIM field on the LEGACY side only (principal or status) -> `FIELD_DIFFERS` / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, with `legacyValue` and `currentValue` both populated and different.
- ABSENT-CURRENT: commit a SUBSET of the corpus durably, then compare against the FULL legacy facts -> `ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT` / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION for the uncommitted entity. This is the arm that proves the current side really came from durable rows: if the suite were building the current projection itself, the entity could not be missing.
- ABSENT-LEGACY: the mirror — compare a reduced legacy fact set against the fully committed store -> `ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_LEGACY` / UNKNOWN. Note the asymmetry is deliberate in the contract: a fact only the new side has is UNKNOWN to this comparison, not a legacy defect, and asserting the disposition is what pins that.
- UNMAPPED-FIELD: a legacy field outside `SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS` -> `FIELD_UNMAPPED` / UNKNOWN, and assert `comparison.refusals` carries ONE typed refusal for it with its exact code and layer. The contract promises one typed refusal per unmapped field precisely so the code is never inferred.
- KNOWN-EMPTY IS NOT A MISMATCH: the `links: []` claim and the HISTORICAL claim must produce ZERO LINK and ZERO BLOCKER mismatches and zero refusals. Collapsing known-empty into unavailable is how a shadow comparison starts inventing or hiding reconciliation work; assert the absence as a fact.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 5 — MISMATCH ARMS GREEN. `Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 10 passed (10)`. Every arm asserts the exact mismatch kind AND its disposition, and every disposition is LOOKED UP in `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS` rather than hand-asserted.

- CHANGED -> `FIELD_DIFFERS` / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, with `legacyValue` and `currentValue` both non-null AND different. Asserting both sides populated is what separates a genuine difference from an absence wearing the wrong kind.
- ABSENT-CURRENT -> `ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT` / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, `currentValue` null. Built by committing a SUBSET to the real store and deriving the FULL legacy facts through the same production chain against a scratch store. This is the arm that proves the current side really came from durable rows — a suite building that side itself could not produce an absence at all.
- ABSENT-LEGACY -> `ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_LEGACY` / UNKNOWN, `legacyValue` null. Asserted BOTH against the production map and against the literal `"UNKNOWN"`, because the asymmetry is the contract's own decision: a fact only the NEW side has is unknown to this comparison, not a legacy defect.
- KNOWN-EMPTY -> zero LINK and zero BLOCKER mismatches and zero refusals, plus the absence asserted as a POSITIVE fact: exactly ONE blocker exists in the current projection (the SUSPENDED claim's) and at least one HISTORICAL claim is present. Asserting only "no mismatches" would also pass if the projection were empty.

=== A PLAN EXPECTATION THAT MEASUREMENT DISPROVED — the unmapped-field arm ===
The plan expects `FIELD_UNMAPPED` / UNKNOWN out of the comparison plus one typed refusal. **That kind is UNREACHABLE through `compareImportShadow` with any honest corpus**, and I confirmed it three ways rather than inferring it:
1. STRUCTURAL: `compareFields` (shadow-projection.ts:182-195) reports unmapped only when a field key falls outside `fieldsFor(kind)`. Both sides' entities are built by production mappers that emit exactly the declared keys — `projectLegacyImport` (:60-77) for the legacy side, the daemon mapper (import-shadow-mapper.ts:68-84) for the current side. Neither can emit an extra key.
2. UPSTREAM: an unmapped payload key never becomes a projection field at all. `applyImport`'s `claimFrom` reads only owner/held/parent/dependsOn; anything else is handled against `knownFields` as a RECONCILIATION FINDING.
3. PROBED on a corpus carrying `unmappedThing`: `ok=true | mismatchKinds=[] | refusalCodes=[]`. Probe deleted in the same command, residue verified empty.
Reaching `FIELD_UNMAPPED` would require hand-assembling a `ShadowProjection` with an extra key — which DoD 1 and task rail 1 forbid outright. So the plan's step-5 unmapped arm and the task's own rail 1 are in direct conflict, and rail 1 wins.

WHAT I WROTE INSTEAD, because "unreachable" is not a reason to cover nothing: an arm that pins the BOUNDARY. It asserts the importer DID record a reconciliation finding naming `unmappedThing` (so the field really was unmapped and really was noticed), then asserts the shadow comparison invents nothing downstream — no mismatch, no refusal — and that no entity on either side carries the key. That is a genuine regression guard: it fails if a future change either drops the upstream finding or starts manufacturing a downstream verdict for a field the comparison never saw. The case-table row was corrected from `mismatch("FIELD_UNMAPPED")` to a new `ABSORBED_UPSTREAM` outcome with the measurement recorded beside it, because leaving the old row would have declared an expectation nothing can satisfy.

HARNESS EXTENDED MINIMALLY: `IngestResult` now surfaces `reconciliations` from the committed `ImportReport`, so the boundary arm reads the importer's own finding rather than re-deriving one.

STILL NO PROJECTION CONSTRUCTED ANYWHERE. Every arm supplies legacy facts the importer derived and reads the adapter's verdict. The ABSENT arms use `openScratchStore` — a second REAL project-bound store — rather than a stub port, so the full production chain runs on both sides of every comparison.

STEP 6 — REFUSAL ARMS GREEN. `Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 18 passed (18)`. Every arm pins the exact stable code AND which layer answered, and every arm re-measures the store afterwards.

AT `DAEMON_IMPORT_SHADOW`, six arms, one per branch of `readImportShadowProjection`:
- `manifestDigest: "NOT-A-DIGEST"` -> `IMPORT_SHADOW_INPUT_INVALID`.
- a well-formed digest with no committed aggregate -> `IMPORT_SHADOW_ABSENT`, plus an explicit `not.toBe("IMPORT_SHADOW_INPUT_INVALID")`: the shape was fine and the import simply was not there, and collapsing those two would hide a real operator distinction.
- `readEvents` THROWS -> `IMPORT_SHADOW_STORE_UNREADABLE`, asserted as a returned refusal rather than a propagated throw.
- `readEvents` answers a NON-LIST (`{length: 3}`) -> also `IMPORT_SHADOW_STORE_UNREADABLE`. This is the arm the adapter's own comment demands: the shape check sits inside the catch's reach because a port answering a non-list would otherwise crash on `.length`, and **a crash is not a refusal** — it carries no code, no layer and no evidence about which row was bad.
- HORIZON MOVES between the two reads -> `IMPORT_SHADOW_HORIZON_DRIFT`, asserting `horizonCalls > 1` (so the adapter genuinely re-read rather than the fixture faking a single call) and `not.toHaveProperty("comparison")` — no partial comparison escapes, because a projection assembled across two states is a mixture of both.
- HOSTILE LEGACY FACTS (`{claims: null, links: null}`) -> `IMPORT_SHADOW_LEGACY_UNREADABLE`, with no comparison returned. The legacy side is CALLER data — bytes someone read out of a frozen project — which is exactly why `compareImportShadow` wraps `projectLegacyImport` in a try/catch.

=== THE TWO ARMS THAT PROVE CODES ARE NOT RESTAMPED ===
`scanEvents` forwards the decoder's own verdict verbatim (`forwardRefusal`, import-shadow-reader.ts:112) so malformed bytes stay distinguishable from an unsupported schema. Both arms plant a row directly under `legacy-import:<digest>` in a scratch store, which is the only honest way to reach a corrupted durable row — `commitLegacyImport` only ever writes what the importer drafted.
- TAMPERED PAYLOAD -> the refusal's code `startsWith("IMPORT_EVENT_")` and its layer is asserted **NOT** to be `IMPORT_SHADOW_READ_LAYER`. That is the importer's own vocabulary reaching the caller intact.
- UNSUPPORTED ENVELOPE SCHEMA -> `IMPORT_SHADOW_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` at `IMPORT_SHADOW_READ_LAYER`, because the ENVELOPE is the daemon's own concern.
The pair is the point: two adjacent failures, two different layers, and the assertions would fail if either layer started answering for the other. A suite asserting only `ok === false` would stay green through exactly that regression.

DoD 4 ENFORCED ON EVERY REFUSAL, not just at the end. `expectStoreUntouched` re-reads raw event count, command-decision count, database size and database mtime after each arm and requires all four unchanged. A handler that refused AFTER writing is completely invisible to a return-value assertion, which is why this is measured rather than argued from `ImportShadowStorePort` declaring only two readers.

ADVISORY POSTURE IS ASSERTED ON THE REFUSED ARM TOO — `advisoryOnly: true`, `authority: "NONE"` — inside the shared `refused()` helper, so it cannot be forgotten per-arm. Step 8 extends this to the accepted arm and to the no-activation check.

The `refused()` helper reports what came back when a refusal was expected but a comparison arrived, and `compared()` reports the refusal's own code and layer when the reverse happens — so a broken arm names production's actual answer instead of "expected true to be false".

implementationPlan.description:
DETERMINISM AND PROVENANCE — DoD item 3.
- SOURCE COMMIT: capture `git rev-parse HEAD` ONCE at suite start and record it on every case result. Assert every case carries that same commit; a matrix whose halves ran against different trees is comparing two systems.
- FIXTURE MANIFEST DIGEST: record the canonical manifest digest `buildSourceManifest` derived for the corpus on every case, and assert it is stable across cases that share a corpus. The digest is the importer's own, never recomputed here — recomputing it would be a second derivation that can disagree with the one the events were committed under.
- IDENTICAL ORDERED BYTES: run the entire matrix twice over unchanged corpus bytes in one process and assert the ordered comparison output serializes byte-identically. The comparator has no clock and no random source and its mismatch order is total, so any instability is a real defect rather than expected noise. If some field is genuinely environment-dependent, exclude it BY NAME with a comment — never by comparing a subset, which passes every gate while proving nothing.
- Also assert the two runs produced the same number of mismatches per case, so a difference cannot hide inside a serialization that happens to sort equal.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 7 — DETERMINISM AND PROVENANCE GREEN. `Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 21 passed (21)`. DoD 3 covered on all three clauses.

SOURCE COMMIT captured ONCE at suite scope via `execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"])`, rooted at the repo via `import.meta.dirname` rather than at the process cwd — vitest's cwd is not guaranteed to be the repo root, and a `git` call that resolved somewhere else would silently record a different tree's commit. Asserted to match `/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/` and then asserted identical on EVERY case record. A matrix whose halves ran against different trees is comparing two systems, and that is invisible without this.

MANIFEST DIGEST is the IMPORTER's own, taken from the committed `ImportReport` and never recomputed locally. A local recomputation would be a second derivation free to disagree with the one the events were actually committed under — the same class of defect as a second vocabulary. Asserted stable across every case sharing a corpus (`digests.size === 1`) and shaped `/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/`.

BYTE-IDENTICAL ORDERED OUTPUT: the whole matrix runs TWICE in one process over unchanged corpus bytes, and each case's `JSON.stringify(result.comparison)` must be byte-identical between runs. **Nothing is excluded from the serialization.** The comparator has no clock and no random source and its mismatch order is total, so I had no environment-dependent field to exclude — and the plan is right that excluding by subset would pass every gate while proving nothing. If a field ever does become environment-dependent, it must be excluded BY NAME with a comment rather than by comparing a slice.

THREE GUARDS AGAINST A VACUOUS "IDENTICAL", because two empty strings also compare equal:
- `mismatchCount` asserted equal per case ALONGSIDE the serialization, so a difference cannot hide inside a serialization that happens to sort equal.
- `manifestDigest` asserted equal per case.
- `first.some((record) => record.mismatchCount > 0)` — at least one case in the pass must genuinely carry mismatches. Without it, a matrix that produced nothing at all would satisfy every determinism assertion above it.
The `runMatrix` helper deliberately includes a SUBSET variant (the absent-current shape) precisely so that last assertion has something to be true about; a determinism check over only the exact-match control would compare two empty mismatch lists.

Each pass builds a fresh temp corpus and fresh stores, so "unchanged bytes" means the same CONTENT rather than the same files — which is the stronger claim, since it also shows the digest and the comparison do not depend on the temp path they happen to sit under.

implementationPlan.description:
THE UNTOUCHED-BYTES PROOF — DoD item 4, and the claim the task title is really about.
Assert on BYTES rather than on promises, for the copied corpus and for the durable store, across EVERY arm including refusals:
- CORPUS: the AFTER inventory equals the BEFORE inventory entry-for-entry — SHA-256, size and mtime for every file. Include the mtime deliberately: an accidental write-mode open that restores identical content still moves it, and that is the only signal of it.
- STORE: raw event count, command-decision count, database file size and database mtime unchanged across every read and every comparison. `ImportShadowStorePort` declares only two readers, so a write is not merely unexpected — it is unrepresentable through the port the adapter holds; assert it anyway, because the suite hands the adapter a REAL store and the guarantee is about what the adapter does with it.
- ADVISORY POSTURE (task rail 3): assert every accepted result carries `advisoryOnly: true` and `authority: "NONE"` on BOTH arms as the contract promises, and that nothing in the matrix activates imported state, selects a best tool, or performs a cutover. Assert the returned object exposes no method that could.
- Prove the inventory itself can fail: as a positive control, deliberately touch one corpus file in a scratch copy and confirm the comparison reports it. An inventory that cannot detect a change is a green light wired to nothing.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 8 — UNTOUCHED-BYTES PROOF GREEN. `Test Files 1 passed (1) | Tests 24 passed (24)`. This is the claim the task title is really about, and it is asserted on BYTES rather than on promises.

THE BASELINES ARE TAKEN AFTER INGEST, deliberately. The importer is ALLOWED to write — that is its job — so a baseline captured before the commit would fail for the right reason at the wrong moment and prove nothing about the reader. Captured after ingest, the assertion isolates exactly what this task certifies: the SHADOW READ touches nothing.

ONE ARM EXERCISES FIVE CALLS against the same real store — the accepted comparison plus refusals for INPUT_INVALID, ABSENT, LEGACY_UNREADABLE and STORE_UNREADABLE — and only then re-measures. Both inventories are compared with `toEqual` entry-for-entry (digest AND size AND mtime for every file), and the store is compared on raw event count, decision count, database size and database mtime. A refusal that wrote before refusing is invisible to a return-value assertion, which is why this runs after the refusals rather than only after the happy path.

`ImportShadowStorePort` declares only `readEventHorizon` and `readEvents`, so a write is not merely unexpected — it is UNREPRESENTABLE through the port the adapter holds. I measured it anyway, because the suite hands the adapter a REAL `SqliteEventStore` and the guarantee that matters is about what the adapter DOES with it, not about what its parameter type would permit.

THE INVENTORY POSITIVE CONTROL is the assertion I care most about here. It appends one byte to one corpus file in a scratch copy and requires the inventory to SEE it: the whole inventory differs, that file's digest differs, that file's size differs — and every OTHER entry is still identical, so the control is specific rather than "something somewhere moved". Without this, every "untouched" assertion above is a green light wired to nothing; an inventory that silently returned `{}` would satisfy all of them.

ADVISORY POSTURE (task rail 3) asserted on BOTH arms — `advisoryOnly: true`, `authority: "NONE"` on the accepted result and on a refusal — plus three structural checks that nothing here could activate anything:
- the returned object is frozen;
- it exposes NO function-valued property (`methods` is empty), so there is no method a caller could invoke to activate, cut over, or pick a winner;
- every mismatch disposition is one of the two advisory arms, `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION` or `UNKNOWN`. `ShadowComparison` has no third arm to widen into, and asserting the closed set is what would catch one being added.

Nothing in the matrix activates imported state, selects a best tool, or performs a cutover — and that is now enforced by the shape of the returned value rather than by reading the implementation and trusting it.

planningNotes.risks:
1) THE TAUTOLOGY IS THE FAILURE MODE THAT MATTERS. If the current side is ever derived from `projectLegacyImport`, this matrix compares one function with itself and reports agreement forever while fully green. Drill #1 and the ABSENT-CURRENT case (which is impossible unless the current side really came from durable rows) are the two independent defences; keep both.

If it has been reverted, the current side must fall back to seeding through `applyImport` plus a real store port, and the completion notes must say so — do not silently change strategy.

3) KNOWN-EMPTY vs UNAVAILABLE is the semantic hinge the adapter was built around. `links: []` and a HISTORICAL claim mean ZERO LINK and ZERO BLOCKER entities and a successful read. A corpus that never contains those two shapes cannot see a regression in the distinction, which is why step 2 mandates them.

4) TWO LAYERS CAN REFUSE, and asserting only `ok === false` would stay green if the daemon layer started answering first and swallowed the importer's finer code. Every refusal arm pins the layer.

5) mtime IS PART OF THE READ-ONLY PROOF. A write-mode open that restores identical content leaves digest and size unchanged; only mtime moves. Capture all three for every corpus entry, and prove the inventory can actually fail via the positive control in step 8.

6) `SqliteEventStore.open` vs `openForProject`: the former refuses every commit with PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED. Getting this wrong makes ingest fail in a way that reads like an importer defect.

7) SHARED DIRECTORY. task-efe5465f owns three other files under tests/integration/portability. Do not edit them, and expect their churn in a repo-wide baseline.

8) `pnpm test:integration` MUST RUN FROM POWERSHELL (MSYS tar / drive-letter paths), and tests/integration is typechecked by nothing — both are gate hazards rather than code hazards, and both are easy to skip without noticing.

9) RESOURCE RESIDUE: temp trees, real SQLite files and copied corpora on every case. Run the suite twice in one command; a teardown that has only ever run once has not been tested.
